lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The study was locked from the inside. The key lay on the desk.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He never opened the door.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Aldous Crane, a publisher, went into his study at nine. At half past ten, he had not come out.

lines.speaker: Inspector Dale
lines.text: Mara knocked for ten minutes. Then we forced the door.

lines.speaker: Inspector Dale
lines.text: The window latch was shut. The only key was on his desk. Nobody could have gone in or out.

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.text: That's impossible, Kiri.

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: Nothing is impossible. Something is just hidden.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Kiri was twelve, and he rarely spoke. He looked at things the way other people listen.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He walked the room once. The desk. The key. The clock on the shelf. The door.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The desk was tidy. A cold cup of tea. A manuscript with a red pencil on top.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: And a thin gap at the top of the door, no wider than a coin.

lines.speaker: Inspector Dale
lines.text: Crane's wristwatch stopped at nine-forty. So we think that is when it happened.

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: Stopped. But the clock on the shelf is still running.

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.text: So? Different clocks.

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: Remember that. Remember the watch.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Three people were in the house that night. Each of them has an alibi.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: First, Dr. Voss, Crane's doctor. He came at nine for a check-up and left the study at twenty past.

lines.speaker: Dr. Voss
lines.text: He was well. Cheerful, even. I said goodnight in the hall.

lines.speaker: Dr. Voss
lines.text: At nine-forty I phoned the hospital from this very phone. The switchboard keeps a log.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A bag of medicine bottles, a spool of blue thread, a stick of red sealing wax. A doctor's tools.

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.text: A phone log. That's solid.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Second, Mara, the secretary. She has worked for Crane for six years.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: From nine to ten I counted the silver with Mrs. Pell, the cook. We never left the kitchen.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: He told me to take the morning off. He said he would write me a letter.

lines.speaker: Mara
lines.text: He never said what was in it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The cook agrees. Mara found the door locked at half past ten and called the police.

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.text: Another alibi. Everyone is covered.

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: Not yet. Keep counting.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Third, Felix, Crane's nephew. He has money troubles, and an uncle who refused to help.

lines.speaker: Felix
lines.text: We argued at supper. I left at ten to nine and walked straight to the cinema.

lines.speaker: Inspector Dale
lines.text: A man with a motive and an alibi. Interesting.

lines.speaker: Felix
lines.text: I was at the village cinema from nine. Here is my ticket. The usher saw me all night.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The ticket says nine o'clock. The usher confirms it.

lines.speaker: Inspector Dale
lines.text: Three people, three alibis, one locked room. I do not like it, Kiri.

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: I do. It means someone made a plan.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Now look closely. Three clues are in plain view. Each one is named once.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Nobody touched the room. The police photographed everything, and the three clues sat there the whole time.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: One. A tiny drop of red wax on the door frame, level with the lock.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Two. A blue fibre caught on the ring of the key.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Three. A wristwatch stopped at nine-forty, glass unbroken, while the clock on the shelf still runs.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Pause the video if you want to guess. Who made a plan?

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: The wax first. The only red sealing wax in this house is in one bag.

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: And nobody drips wax on a door frame by accident.

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.text: The doctor's bag?

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: Let's see what else it explains.

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: The fibre. Not wool, not cotton. Blue nylon thread, the kind in a spool.

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: A spool like the one in the doctor's bag. Mara's drawer has only white thread. Felix owns none.

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.text: So the thread touched the key.

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: And the key was never in the lock. Why would a thread go through its ring?

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: Now the watch. Stopped at nine-forty, with an unbroken glass.

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: A fall would crack it. So someone stopped it by hand, and chose the time.

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: Who needs it to be nine-forty? Only someone who is safe at nine-forty.

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: Felix was in the cinema from nine. Mara was in the kitchen from nine. They are safe at any hour that matters.

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: Dr. Voss left the study at twenty past nine. His only alibi starts at nine-forty.

lines.speaker: Inspector Dale
lines.text: So the watch was moved to hide the true time.

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: Here is how the door was locked. Step one. A latch bar inside the door, lifted, with a thread tied to it.

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: Step two. The thread runs through the ring of the key.

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: Then it passes over a drop of wax, a small guide, and out through the gap above the door.

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: Step three. Outside, pull the thread. The key is a weight. The bar drops, and the door is fast.

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: Step four. Let go. The thread slips out through the gap, dragged by the falling key, which lands on the desk.

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: It leaves a fibre on the ring, and a drop of wax on the frame.

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.text: A harmless trick with a thread, a weight and a bar. And all of it was in plain view.

lines.speaker: Inspector Dale
lines.text: So the door was never locked from inside at all.

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: It only looked locked. Anyone can fool a door. It is much harder to fool a clock.

lines.speaker: Inspector Dale
lines.text: Dr. Voss, open your bag.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The spool was blue. The thread matched the fibre. The wax matched the drop.

lines.speaker: Dr. Voss
lines.text: This is ridiculous. I was on the phone at nine-forty.

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: You were. But Mr. Crane was already silent, and the clock on the shelf is the only honest clock in the room.

lines.speaker: Dr. Voss
lines.text: A thread? Half the village owns blue thread!

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: Half the village does not own that wax. Or a watch that stops at the very hour you need.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The motive is two lines long. Crane was about to print a story about Voss.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It said the work that made the doctor famous was never his own.

lines.speaker: Inspector Dale
lines.text: Dr. Voss confessed in the hall. Mara cried, and Felix could not speak.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He did not want the world to read it. So he planned a door nobody could open.

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.text: All because of a thread.

lines.speaker: Kiri
lines.text: Which clue did you notice first?

scenes.title: The locked door
scenes.place: A shadowy hallway outside a heavy oak study door, a brass lamp glowing at the far end

scenes.title: The study
scenes.place: Inside Aldous Crane's study, a dark wooden desk with a lamp, a brass key on a green blotter, a clock ticking on the shelf

scenes.title: Dr. Voss
scenes.place: The grand hallway of Crane's house at night, a medical bag on a chair beside a hall telephone

scenes.title: Mara
scenes.place: A busy farmhouse kitchen at night, a cook stirring a pot, silver spoons laid out on a long table

scenes.title: Felix
scenes.place: A small village cinema lobby, a ticket booth, a red ticket stub in a young man's hand

scenes.title: Three clues
scenes.place: A close view of the study door frame and the desk, with a magnifying glass hovering over a tiny spot of red wax

scenes.title: The wax
scenes.place: A close view of the door frame, a drop of red wax shining beside a small iron latch bar

scenes.title: The thread
scenes.place: A close view of the brass key on the green blotter, a single blue fibre across its ring

scenes.title: The watch
scenes.place: A close view of Crane's silver wristwatch on the desk, the hands stopped, the glass shining and whole

scenes.title: The trick
scenes.place: A re-enactment drawing of the study door from the outside, a long blue thread running from the latch bar through a key ring to a wax guide on the frame

scenes.title: The hall
scenes.place: The hallway again at dawn, the medical bag open on a chair and a spool of blue thread on top

scenes.title: Why
scenes.place: A quiet study at sunrise, a manuscript on the desk with a single page lifted by the draught
